title: 87 published labels resolve to more than one identifier, including 18 preferred_term-vs-synonym collisions
body:
Found reviewing #231, which introduces the ambiguity by publishing synonyms.

Before #231, `docs/data/*.csv` carried only `preferred_term`, and **preferred_terms are unique** (verified: zero duplicates). So the CSV supported an unambiguous `{label: identifier}` join. Publishing synonyms makes that join order-dependent for **87 labels**.

The sharp cases are where **one record's `preferred_term` is another record's synonym** — a consumer's answer depends purely on row order:

| label | holders |
|---|---|
| `Vitamin B12` | CHEBI:176843 (preferred) / CHEBI:17439 (synonym) / UNMAPPED_0005 (synonym) |
| `Mannitol` | CHEBI:29864 (preferred) / CHEBI:16899 (synonym) |
| `Tryptophan` | CHEBI:27897 (preferred) / CHEBI:16828 (synonym) |
| `Citrate` | CHEBI:16947 (preferred) / CHEBI:30769 (synonym) |
| `Sulfur` | CHEBI:26833 (preferred) / CHEBI:17909 (synonym) |
| `Putrescine` | CHEBI:17148 (preferred) / cas:333-93-7 (synonym) |

…and ~12 more of that shape.

Some of these are the #218 family in another guise — `Citrate`/`Citric acid`, `Sulfur`, `Mannitol` are the same substance under two CHEBI ids, i.e. the inverse defect of #225. Others are legitimately shared synonyms where two distinct terms both accept a loose common name.

#231 does **not** treat this as a failure — a synonym legitimately can be shared, and failing the build on it would block the fix. The gate prints it as a note.

## What to decide

1. Which of the 87 are the #225/#218 inverse defect (one substance, two ids) and should be merged, versus genuinely-shared loose names.
2. For the genuine ones, whether the published surface should carry a precedence signal so a consumer can resolve deterministically — e.g. a `match_type` column distinguishing preferred_term from synonym, so `Vitamin B12` → CHEBI:176843 is the documented answer.

Until (2), consumers joining on the `synonyms` column should prefer a row whose `preferred_term` equals the query.

Related: #231, #229, #218, #225.
